tts: In the UAE, there's no income tax. You keep your whole paycheck. So how does a whole country pay its bills?
Answer number one: oil. The UAE is one of the world's biggest producers, and most of it sits under Abu Dhabi.
But that oil money isn't just spent. It's invested. Abu Dhabi's biggest fund alone is estimated at over a trillion dollars, and it pays out every year.
Secret number two: citizens are only about eleven percent of the population. The generous perks go to them. Everyone else is an expat.
And expats pay in other ways. Fees: visas, licenses, fines, toll roads. In Dubai, another five percent of your rent.
And yes, there are taxes: five percent VAT, a nine percent corporate tax, and a hundred percent excise on cigarettes and energy drinks.
Today, over three quarters of the economy isn't oil: trade, tourism, finance. Zero income tax is the bait that pulls in people and money.
sub: Over ¾ of the economy isn't oil

tts: So the UAE does have taxes. They're just not on your paycheck. They're paid in oil, in funds, and on your receipt.
sub: Paid in oil, funds and receipts
